text.p: These are the leading stories in the Angolan press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The U.N. Observer Mission and the observer nations to the peace process, the U.S., Russia and Portugal condemned UNITA for a recent series of incidents where United Nations and aid workers were held against their will by the former rebels.

- Portuguese Economics Minister, Augusto Mateus, met on Monday with the Angolan Minister of Industry, Manuel Duque. Mateus is in Luanda on a two-day visit and has already met with representatives of the city's state and private banks.
- The Journal, quoting police sources, said UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi planned to re-open old UNITA bases in the south of the country.
